title: Completing a Table of Function Compositions (Set I)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Complete the missing entries in the composition table for g(x), f(x), and (f o g)(x): (a) g(x) = x - 7, f(x) = sqrt(x), (f o g)(x) = ?; (b) g(x) = x + 2, f(x) = 3x, (f o g)(x) = ?; (c) g(x) = ?, f(x) = sqrt(x - 5), (f o g)(x) = sqrt(x^2 - 5); (d) g(x) = x/(x - 1), f(x) = x/(x - 1), (f o g)(x) = ?; (e) g(x) = ?, f(x) = 1 + 1/x, (f o g)(x) = x; (f) g(x) = 1/x, f(x) = ?, (f o g)(x) = x.

steps.title: Solve Parts (a), (b), and (c) by Direct Substitution and Pattern Matching
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} \text{(a) } (f \circ g)(x) &= f(x - 7) = \sqrt{x - 7} \\ \text{(b) } (f \circ g)(x) &= f(x + 2) = 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6 \\ \text{(c) } f(g(x)) &= \sqrt{g(x) - 5} = \sqrt{x^2 - 5} \implies g(x) = x^2 \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: In (a) and (b), substitute g(x) directly into f(x). In (c), comparing sqrt(g(x) - 5) with sqrt(x^2 - 5) shows that g(x) = x^2.
steps.why: Matching the structure of f(g(x)) with the target composite expression determines the inner function g(x).

steps.title: Simplify the Self-Inverse Rational Composition in Part (d)
steps.explanation: Substitute g(x) = x/(x - 1) into f(x) = x/(x - 1) and multiply numerator and denominator by (x - 1) to simplify to x.
steps.why: The function x / (x - 1) is an involution (its own inverse) on R \ {1}.

steps.title: Solve for the Unknown Component Functions in Parts (e) and (f)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} \text{(e) } 1 + \frac{1}{g(x)} &= x \implies \frac{1}{g(x)} = x - 1 \implies g(x) = \frac{1}{x - 1} \\ \text{(f) } f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) &= x = \frac{1}{1/x} \implies f(x) = \frac{1}{x} \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: In (e), solve the equation f(g(x)) = 1 + 1/g(x) = x algebraically for g(x). In (f), since applying f to 1/x returns its reciprocal x, f(x) must be the reciprocal function 1/x.
steps.why: Solving f(g(x)) = x finds the right-inverse g of f in (e) and the left-inverse f of g in (f).
